distractorExplanations.d: Muscle relaxation is primary flaccidity (before rigor) or secondary flaccidity (after rigor passes), not rigor mortis itself.
distractorExplanations.a: Postmortem cooling of the body is algor mortis, not rigor mortis.
distractorExplanations.b: Gravitational settling of blood into dependent areas is livor mortis, not rigor mortis.

options.a: Casket choice and service date ahead of the body's condition
options.b: Condition, cause/manner context, and restoration needs
options.c: A single standard fluid strength for every case
options.d: Cause of death alone, ignoring body condition

distractorExplanations.a: Case analysis evaluates the body's condition first; merchandise and service scheduling do not drive fluid and technique choices.
distractorExplanations.c: Case analysis exists to tailor fluid strength and volume to each body, not to apply one standard solution.
distractorExplanations.d: Cause of death is one factor; case analysis also weighs body condition, edema, discoloration, and restoration needs.

options.a: Whichever adult relative contacts the funeral home first
options.b: The person who signs and pays for the funeral
options.d: State priority of rights / authorizing agent rules

distractorExplanations.a: Custody follows the state priority list (designated agent, spouse, adult children, parents), not which relative calls first.
distractorExplanations.b: Paying for the funeral does not confer the legal right to control disposition under state priority rules.
distractorExplanations.c: The funeral director follows the state's right-of-disposition statute and does not choose the authorizing party.

options.a: Office hours, with first calls left for the next morning
options.c: Peak days, with no overnight on-call
options.d: Arrangements, first calls, services, and prep needs

distractorExplanations.a: Deaths occur around the clock; first calls require 24/7 on-call coverage, not a next-morning response after office hours.
distractorExplanations.b: Removals (first calls) are a core staffing need; leaving them out leaves families and facilities waiting.
distractorExplanations.c: Without overnight on-call coverage, night first calls go unanswered; scheduling covers 24/7 needs.

options.a: Cavity aspiration and trocar button placement
options.b: Cosmetizing only, without wax or filler
options.c: Feature building and wax work for viewing

distractorExplanations.a: Aspiration and placing trocar buttons are steps of cavity embalming, not restorative art techniques for viewing.
distractorExplanations.b: Restorative art goes beyond cosmetics to include wax, filler, and feature reconstruction for viewing.
distractorExplanations.d: Clothing and casket interiors are arrangement and merchandise choices, not restorative art techniques.
